claims.text: Toughness retention in high-entropy alloys is governed by the distribution of nanoscale precipitates formed during heat treatment.
A fine, uniform precipitate dispersion improves toughness.
Fine precipitates improve toughness by deflecting cracks.
Fine precipitates improve toughness by enhancing local plasticity.
Annealing or aging can be used to modify nanoscale precipitate features.
Precipitate size and spatial distribution mediate crack deflection and plastic-energy dissipation.
Fine, uniformly dispersed precipitates hinder crack propagation.
Coarse precipitates act as stress-concentration sites.
Stress concentrations associated with coarse precipitates facilitate brittle failure.
A fine, uniformly distributed precipitate structure will produce higher toughness than the baseline state.
Heat treatments that coarsen precipitates will reduce fracture toughness.
Heat treatments that coarsen precipitates will reduce ductility.
The proposed behavior is limited to alloys without significant grain growth or unwanted phase transformations during processing.
A statistically significant association between fine, uniform precipitates and improved toughness is required for the hypothesis to survive the proposed test.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as having minimal precipitate formation, whereas the stated baseline is a standard heat-treated state with a fine precipitate structure. It is therefore unclear which state is the actual comparison baseline.

The prediction says that a fine, uniformly distributed precipitate structure will improve toughness relative to baseline, but the baseline is itself defined as having a fine precipitate structure. No distinguishing precipitate size, density, or uniformity is specified.

The mediator requires precipitates, which ordinarily constitute a distinct phase, while the boundary requires maintenance of a single-phase microstructure. The intended meaning may be a single-phase matrix containing precipitates, but that qualification is not stated.
